column3: Hebrew has plural “fools”; BSB has a singular fool.
Hebrew names the tongue’s healing and perversity in it; BSB turns both into descriptions of a tongue.
Hebrew has a singular “heart”; BSB has plural “hearts.”
Hebrew has a singular pursuer of righteousness; BSB uses “those who pursue.”
“Lie open” is not explicit in Hebrew, which says they are before the LORD.
Hebrew names the reprover as the object of love and says “go to the wise”; BSB has being reproved and consulting them.
Hebrew has plural fools; BSB has a singular fool.
Hebrew retains “lacking heart” and making one’s walking straight; BSB has lacking judgment and walking a straight path.
“Fitting” is not explicit in the first clause; Hebrew names the answer of his mouth.
Hebrew places Sheol “below”; BSB expresses going down to it.
Hebrew has singular “boundary” and a verb of establishing it; BSB has protecting plural boundaries.
Hebrew describes pleasant words as pure; BSB describes the words of pure people as pleasant to Him.
Hebrew says a good report “makes the bone fat”; BSB has “nourishes the bones.”
